newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - BA to post record nine-month result.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - BA to post record nine-month result.

text.p: British Airways is expected to take the opportunity of celebrating 10 years in the private sector when it reports third quarter results on Monday, with the announcement of another record year so far for profits.
Market forecasts predict that the airline will post headline pre-tax profits of around 570 million stg for the nine months to December 31, up from an all-time high of 534 million a year ago.

But BA is expected to report flat profits of around 100 million stg pre-tax for the third quarter, against 104 million stg last time and analysts say investor attention will be focused on what impact higher fuel prices and the strength of sterling will have on operating profits.

While other European airlines have already complained about the jump in fuel prices, BA is regarded as having tighter control on costs and should also benefit from the rise in value of sterling against the dollar in the last three months of 1996.
The airline says between 60 and 70 percent of its sales are made overseas and the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on costs and sales balance out over the longer term.
But changes in exchange rates usually hit foreign currency costs sooner since most air fares are booked in advance.

"It will be interesting to see what their view is now on fuel costs for the fourth quarter, due to the fact that jet prices have been coming off recently," said Kevin Fogarty, sector analyst at Daiwa Europe.

BA said in November that strong traffic growth and greater productivity would have boosted first half operating profits by 10.5 percent had it not been for an extra 51 million stg on its fuel bill and the impact of a threatened pilots strike in July.

In the event, first half operating profits were down 2.1 percent from a year ago to 512 million stg. However, the pre-tax result rose 9.3 percent to 470 million stg thanks to a lower interest charge, payment of dividends on BA's $400 million investment in estranged U.S. partner USAir and an improved contribution from its 25 percent stake in Australia's Qantas.

For the nine months to December 31, the airline has already reported that scheduled mainline traffic was up 5.9 pct, although a 7.3 pct expansion in capacity meant the average percentage of seats sold -- the load factor -- slipped a percentage point to 73.9 percent of capacity.

But traffic in the third quarter was up 9.1 percent, with the load factor rising to a record 71.2 percent from 70.7 percent a year ago. Premium business and first class traffic grew by 5.9 percent against 9.7 percent growth in the main cabin.
